title: Signal Hopper — Mini Sprint Notes (2026-06-02)
content:
Purpose and quick context:

This doc is a compact synthesis of recent frontline feedback (May 2026 window) targeted at shipping 2–3 low-effort, high-impact patches we can prototype in a single mini-sprint (2 weeks). Goal: reduce customer friction for latency-sensitive chat apps and clarify routing/variant behavior that keeps surfacing in support threads.

Sources and signal hygiene:
- Inputs: top 40 CS tickets (May 1–28), three customer review calls (Fintech X, HealthAI partner, Adtech pilot), Slack thread #cs-field-signals, product telemetry snippets (latency spike logs), and a short in-product survey (n=87).
- Confidence tiers: quotes from enterprise pilots = high; aggregated ticket counts = medium; single-customer feature asks = low unless repeated.

Top recurring customer themes (synthesis):
1) Transparent fallback behavior (freq: high)
   - Problem: when backend capacity constrained, customers observe silent model downgrades (smaller quantized variants) without an obvious signal in the response or logs. Leads to puzzling quality regressions.
   - Representative quote: "We saw a sudden drop in summary quality for ~2 hours; only found out after checking token counts — no indicator it fell back." — Fintech X eng lead
   - Impact: trust hits, regression debugging overhead, elevated CS tickets.

2) Cost-vs-latency knobs are confusing (freq: medium-high)
   - Problem: customers want a single place to tune latency/cost tradeoffs per route (not per model). Current UI exposes batching/quantization separately; engineers want a simple SLO slider + policy.
   - Customer ask: "Can we set a 200ms p95 target and have Redwood suggest batching/quant settings?" — Adtech product manager

3) Short-context cache invalidation surprises (freq: medium)
   - Problem: customers relying on prefix/KV caching report occasional cache misses after autoscaler events / routing changes. Misses correlate with throughput spikes and route failovers.
   - Impact: higher token cost and tail latency spikes for production conversations.

4) Embeddings versioning friction (freq: low-medium but high severity for search use)
   - Problem: mismatch between embedding generation parameters across model upgrades; customers want traceable version IDs attached to embeddings and a migration plan.

Suggested mini-sprint priorities (ranked by effort x impact):
- Quick patch A (1.5 engineer-weeks; high impact): Add explicit fallback metadata to response envelope + console alerting.
  - UX: response header fields (fallback_model_id, fallback_reason, fallback_latency_penalty). Console: per-route timeline highlighting fallback events with counts.
  - Instrumentation: emit structured events to trace pipeline and surface in token-level analytics.
  - Example response addition (proto): {"fallback_model_id": "redwood/gpt-3.2q-lite", "fallback_reason": "capacity-fallback"}
  - Why quick: small change in response layer + console timeline widget reuse.

- Quick patch B (2.5 engineer-weeks; medium-high impact): Route-level SLO slider (suggested config generator).
  - UX: single slider in route config (latency vs cost).
  - Backend: small policy engine that maps slider to batching window + quant profile + prefer-region settings. Populate suggested mapping based on recent telemetry.
  - Why: reduces support questions and aligns behavior across teams.

- Probe C (2 engineer-weeks; exploratory): Cache resilience probe + autoscaler tie-in.
  - Implement a probe harness that simulates autoscaler events and measures cache miss delta. If miss delta > threshold, emit a routing flag to temporarily prefer warmed nodes.
  - Why exploratory: requires SRE coordination and can be disruptive; but solves recurrent customer pain.

Customer-facing framing / messaging:
- For fallbacks: "We are rolling out explicit fallback signals so you can detect and debug model downgrades quickly." Include sample SDK snippet showing how to read fallback headers.
- For SLO slider: beta banner to customers with heavy latency sensitivity + short onboarding guide.

Risks and open questions:
- Instrumentation cost: emitting more structured events increases telemetry volume — need cost estimate from Observability team (See linked artifact GHE PR).
- Backend policy conflicts: Dedicated customers may want stricter controls (no automatic fallback) — how to respect account-level policies?
- Console space: timeline widget reuse likely but check product backlog conflicts with current roadmap.

Proposed acceptance criteria (for each patch):
- Quick patch A: in-production responses include fallback fields for 100% of routed requests in canary accounts; fallback events visible in console timeline; CS ticket volume about fallback-related regressions drops by 60% in pilot customers.
- Quick patch B: SLO slider appears in route config; default mapping suggested by system; 2 pilot accounts adopt slider and report measurable latency improvement or cost reduction in 14 days.

Implementation notes / tiny spec fragments:
- SDK changes: add optional response.fallback metadata accessors in Python/Node SDKs. Backwards compatible; absence indicates no fallback.
- Telemetry schema: event type = "fallback_event_v1" fields = [timestamp, route_id, req_id, original_model, fallback_model, reason, latency_ms].
- Console: timeline filters by route_id + model pair; show counts per day with sample request link.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- T+0 (this doc): sync with Observability (Lena) to estimate telemetry cost (owner: Lena).
- T+1 (2 days): eng triage meeting to size Quick patch A/B and allocate 2sprint-day canary slot (owner: Jasper).
- T+2 (EOW): draft customer beta note for Fintech X and Adtech pilot (owner: Priya).

Pieces to capture in product ticket(s):
- CS-PRIO-FALLBACKS: umbrella ticket for fallback metadata + console work (linked to JIRA-CS-4123).
- CS-PRIO-SLO-SLIDER: ticket for route SLO mapping + UX.

Notes to self / scratch fragments:
- Consider tiny telemetry toggle ("fallback_flags=true") per-account to limit volume during beta.
- Could we repurpose existing "route annotations" to store last-known model-version for quicker diffing?
- Quick UX mock: one-line status pill on route overview: "Fallbacks: 3 today (0 ongoing)".

Appendix: short customer vignettes (aggregate):
- Fintech X: heavy p95 sensitivity; primary ask = explicit signal + SLA for no silent downgrades; willing to trial beta with dedicated logging.
- HealthAI partner: concerned about embedding drift after model upgrades; requests version tags and migration path.
- Adtech pilot: cost pressure; willing to trade small quality delta for predictable 200ms p95 across bursty traffic.
- Tickets snapshot: 42 tickets referencing "downgrade/quality regression" in May; 18 referencing "cache miss after scale".

If anything here looks like the wrong priority to your team, call it out in the triage meeting. My bias: fallback visibility is the fastest lever to restore customer trust and clear a lot of these tickets.

---
Priya Shah
Customer Success — Signal Ops
Notes: pinned for mini-sprint planning (wk of 2026-06-07).
